beats.title: Michael Romanov Elected Tsar
beats.description: An assembly of nobles, clergy and townsmen chose a teenage boy to end years of chaos and found a new ruling dynasty.

beats.title: The Law Code Binds Peasants to Land
beats.description: A sweeping new legal code tied peasants permanently to their landlords' estates, hardening serfdom for two centuries.

beats.title: Ukraine Swears Allegiance to Tsar
beats.description: Cossack leaders meeting at Pereyaslav accepted the tsar's protection, drawing a huge part of Ukraine into his realm.

beats.title: Council Condemns the Old Believers
beats.description: A church council backed liturgical reforms and cursed those who refused them, splitting Russian Orthodoxy for good.
beats.note: Council ran 1666-67 with the anathema in 1667; year it began used.

beats.title: Two Boy Tsars Share the Throne
beats.description: After a bloody revolt by the palace guards, a young boy and his half-brother were crowned together with their sister as regent.

beats.title: Treaty of Nerchinsk with China
beats.description: Russia and the Qing empire fixed their first border along the Amur region, opening a long period of caravan trade.

beats.title: Peter Becomes Sole Tsar
beats.description: When his co-ruler died, Peter ruled alone, and the same year his army seized the Turkish fortress of Azov.
beats.note: Ivan V died 1696; Azov captured same year.

beats.title: Tsar Travels Incognito to Europe
beats.description: Peter toured Dutch and English shipyards and workshops in disguise, hoping to learn the skills Russia lacked.

beats.title: St Petersburg Is Founded
beats.description: Peter began building a new city on marshy Baltic land as a showpiece port and 'window on the West'.

beats.title: Battle of Poltava
beats.description: Peter's army crushed the invading Swedes in Ukraine, ending Sweden's dominance and making Russia a great power.

beats.title: Peter Proclaimed Emperor
beats.description: With peace made with Sweden after a long war, the Senate gave Peter the title of Emperor of all Russia.
beats.note: One site says 1722; most sources, including Russia's presidential library, say 1721.

beats.title: Anna Rips Up the Nobles' Terms
beats.description: A new empress, offered the crown on terms limiting her power, publicly ripped up the deal and ruled as an autocrat.

beats.title: Elizabeth Seizes the Throne
beats.description: Peter's daughter led guards regiments in a bloodless coup against an infant ruler and his German-influenced regency.

beats.title: Moscow University Opens
beats.description: Russia's first university was founded on the advice of a scholar-poet, a lasting centre of learning in the old capital.

beats.title: Catherine Seizes the Throne
beats.description: A German-born princess overthrew her unpopular husband with the guards' help and began a long reign.

beats.title: The Hermitage Collection Begins
beats.description: The empress bought a Berlin merchant's trove of paintings, the seed of what became one of the world's great museums.

beats.title: First Partition of Poland
beats.description: Russia, Prussia and Austria carved off slices of the weakened Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

beats.title: Russia Annexes Crimea
beats.description: The empress absorbed the Crimean Khanate, gaining warm-water Black Sea ports for her fleet.

beats.title: Catherine the Great Dies
beats.description: The long-reigning empress suffered a stroke and died, passing the crown to her estranged son Paul.

beats.title: Tsar Paul Is Murdered
beats.description: Conspirators killed the unpopular emperor in his palace bedroom, and his son Alexander took the throne.

beats.title: Treaty of Tilsit
beats.description: After a defeat, the tsar and Napoleon met on a raft on a river and agreed a short-lived alliance dividing Europe.

beats.title: Napoleon Invades Russia
beats.description: The Grande Armee crossed the border and fought at Borodino, then marched on a burning Moscow before a ruinous retreat.

beats.title: Russian Troops Enter Paris
beats.description: The tsar rode at the head of allied armies into the French capital, which fell and ended Napoleon's first reign.

beats.title: The Decembrist Revolt
beats.description: Liberal-minded army officers led troops onto a square in the capital to oppose a new tsar, and were crushed.

beats.title: Russia's First Railway Opens
beats.description: A short line carried passengers from the capital to the imperial residence, launching steam travel in the empire.

beats.title: The Crimean War Begins
beats.description: Russia's clash with the Ottomans drew in Britain and France, and led to a long siege of Sevastopol.

beats.title: Tsar Frees the Serfs
beats.description: A sweeping decree ended bondage for tens of millions of peasants, the centrepiece of the Tsar Liberator's reforms.

beats.title: Russia Sells Alaska
beats.description: The empire sold its North American territory to the United States for a few million dollars.

beats.title: War and Peace Is Completed
beats.description: Tolstoy's vast novel of the struggle against Napoleon finished publication in book form, a landmark of world literature.

beats.title: Russia Declares War on the Ottomans
beats.description: Backing Balkan Christians, the empire went to war with Turkey, a conflict that carved new states out of the Balkans.

beats.title: Alexander II Is Assassinated
beats.description: Revolutionaries threw bombs at the reforming tsar's carriage in the capital, killing him and ending his liberal course.

beats.title: The First Faberge Imperial Egg
beats.description: A jeweller made a jewelled Easter egg with a hidden golden hen for the tsar's wife, starting a famed annual tradition.

beats.title: Trans-Siberian Railway Begun
beats.description: Work started on a giant rail line to link Moscow with the Pacific, with the future tsar laying a ceremonial first stone.

beats.title: Nicholas II Becomes Tsar
beats.description: On his father's early death, a young and uncertain heir took the throne, last of the line to rule.

beats.title: War with Japan Breaks Out
beats.description: A surprise torpedo attack on Port Arthur began a conflict that ended in humiliating defeats for the empire.

beats.title: Bloody Sunday
beats.description: Troops fired on a peaceful crowd of workers marching to petition the tsar, igniting a nationwide revolution.

beats.title: The First Duma Meets
beats.description: Russia's first elected parliament assembled, only to be dissolved by the tsar within weeks.

beats.title: Russia Enters the Great War
beats.description: Mobilising to defend Serbia, the empire went to war with Germany and Austria, beginning a disastrous conflict.
beats.why_in: WWI entry that doomed the dynasty

beats.title: Rasputin Is Murdered
beats.description: Nobles poisoned, shot and drowned the mystic who held sway over the imperial family and its court.

beats.title: Nicholas II Abdicates
beats.description: Amid strikes and mutinies in the capital, the last tsar gave up his throne, ending three centuries of dynastic rule.
